newsitem.title: USA: ProSource sinks on second day of trading.
newsitem.headline: ProSource sinks on second day of trading.

text.p: ProSource Inc tumbled almost 20 percent on its second day of trading after its $47.6 million initial public offering, off 2-3/8 to 11-3/4.

ProSource distributes food to chain restaurants including Burger King, TGI Friday's and Wendy's. It went public yesterday in an IPO of 3.4 million shares, which priced at $14 each, the low end of their IPO pricing range of $14 to $16.
The shares closed up on 1/8 on Tuesday. Morgan Stanley was the lead underwriter of the offering.
ProSource treasurer Paul Garcia said the company did not comment on its stock price.
One IPO analyst said although he did not know the reason for the decline, he had advised clients to avoid the IPO.

"This company is valued at an enormous premium, and it's by and large an acquisition play," said Manish Shah of the IPO Maven. It hasn't made money in years and they are heavily in debt. I'm actually surprised the deal got done".
Although ProSource was profitable in its first six months of operation in 1992, it posted net losses in 1993, 1994 and 1995, according to regulatory filings.
For 1996, ProSource posted a net loss of $18.0 million including charges for the first six months and expects a loss for the full year.
The company said it would use $21.8 million of proceeds from the offering to pay down part of its $144.6 million of debt outstanding at June 29, 1996.
Because ProSource went public only Tuesday, no analysts have begun coverage yet of the company.
